memos.headline: MSFT and JPM Lead on Relative Strength; UNH in Freefall, AAPL and XOM Lagging
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market across our universe today. MSFT is the standout, up +16.7% over four weeks with RSI at 72 and trading 12.5% above its 50-day mean — strong momentum but approaching overbought territory, so I'd want to see a pullback toward the 50-day before adding aggressively. JPM is the cleanest trend: +13% over 26 weeks, only 9.8% off its 52w high, above both moving averages, and relative strength roughly flat to SPY over 12 weeks — a rare combination of strength and composure. On the avoid side, UNH is in a structural breakdown: RSI 25.7, down 36% from its high, 26.6% below its 200-day mean, and underperforming SPY by 31.6% over four weeks — I see no reason to step in front of that until price reclaims at least the 50-day average. AAPL and XOM are both below their 50- and 200-day means with negative relative strength, and I'd need AAPL above ~215 (its 50-day area) and XOM above ~110 to reconsider.

views.note: Strongest 4w and 12w relative strength in the universe (+11.1% and +11.5% vs SPY), but RSI 72 warrants waiting for a dip toward the 50-day; a close below 390 would negate the thesis.
Cleanest uptrend: +13% over 26w, above both moving averages, low ATR of 2.47%, and only 9.8% off highs; would reassess on a close below 240.
RSI 25.7, down 36% from 52w high, 18.7% below 50d mean — a textbook breakdown with no sign of stabilization; need a sustained move above 440 to reconsider.
Trading 4.7% below 50d and 9.6% below 200d with negative relative strength vs SPY over all timeframes; needs to reclaim ~215 to turn neutral.
Negative 4w relative strength of -11.1% vs SPY, below both moving averages, RSI 45.7 — weak and getting weaker; need a close above 110 to reconsider.
Bouncing with +12.5% over 4w but still 8.5% below 200d and 23.4% off highs; trend is ambiguous until price clears ~125 convincingly.
Middling setup: RSI 56.5, slightly above 50d mean but 4.4% below 200d; 12w relative strength of -8.1% vs SPY keeps me sidelined until a breakout above 175.
Modest 4w bounce of +6.5% but still 21.5% off highs and 12w relative strength of -13.4% vs SPY is among the worst in the group; watching 200 as a key level.

Recent 1w pop of +5.6% brings it back near the 50d mean but still 9.5% below 200d and 22.4% off highs; need a close above 340 to get constructive.

memos.headline: MSFT, GOOGL, and NVDA Show Durable Earnings Power; PG and XOM Face Top-Line Headwinds
memos.body: I see the clearest fundamental strength in MSFT (Q3 revenue +13.3% YoY, net margin 36.9%, net income +17.7%), GOOGL (Q1 revenue +12.0%, net margin 38.3%, net income +46.0%), and NVDA (Q4 revenue +77.9%, net margin 56.2%), all demonstrating expanding or elevated margins alongside double-digit-plus revenue growth. AMZN's margin expansion to 10.7% with net income nearly doubling is encouraging, though I want to see whether AWS and advertising can sustain that trajectory before gaining full conviction. On the weaker end, PG posted revenue -2.1% YoY with flat net income, and XOM saw revenue -1.1% with a thin 9.1% net margin—neither profile supports paying up. A deterioration in MSFT's Intelligent Cloud segment growth or a compression in NVDA's gross margin below 50% would change my view on those names.

views.note: Revenue +13.3% YoY, net margin 36.9%, net income +17.7%—broad-based growth across segments with expanding profitability and manageable $42.9B debt.
Q1 net margin hit 38.3% with revenue +12.0% and net income +46.0% YoY on only $14.8B total debt, the best margin-leverage combo in the universe.
56.2% net margin and 78% revenue growth are extraordinary, though I temper confidence slightly given cyclicality risk in data-center capex.
Net income nearly doubled YoY to $20B on 10.5% revenue growth, but 10.7% net margin is still thin relative to peers and needs confirmation of durability.
Solid 32.3% net margin and +9.1% net income growth, but $407B total debt and macro sensitivity to credit cycle keep me neutral.
29.2% net margin is healthy but only +4.0% revenue growth signals mature hardware saturation; I need to see services mix accelerate.
Revenue declined 5.0% YoY yet net income rose 4.4% on margin discipline (17.2%), but top-line contraction limits upside conviction.
Revenue +6.8% but net margin only 5.5% and net income +1.6%—thin profitability and $76.9B debt leave little room for error.
Revenue -2.1% YoY with flat earnings and a 19.1% margin that could compress further if volumes don't recover.
Revenue -1.1%, net margin 9.1%, and essentially flat net income—commodity headwinds and $36.8B debt make this unattractive on fundamentals.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Benign CPI — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, while the effective rate has drifted down only 15bp over the same window, confirming no active easing. CPI is running at +2.4% y/y — close enough to target that it does not force the Fed's hand — but unemployment has crept up 30bp over the past year to 4.2%, signaling a mild labor-market softening that could tilt the next move toward a cut. The 10y yield at 4.33% has fallen 25bp over three months and the 2s10s curve has steepened 88bp over the past year to +55bp, consistent with the market pricing eventual easing and a late-cycle growth deceleration. In this pause-tilting-toward-easing regime I favor duration-sensitive mega-cap growth (MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL) and defensive staples (PG), while I am cautious on deep cyclicals (CAT) and energy (XOM) that need accelerating nominal growth. A surprise uptick in core CPI above 3% or a payrolls print showing unemployment dropping back below 4% would flip my regime call back to prolonged-hold/hawkish.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and a Fed poised to ease; 10y down 25bp in 3m supports multiples.
Same duration tailwind as MSFT; benign 2.4% CPI keeps real rates from re-accelerating.
Pause-to-easing regime and steepening curve historically support quality mega-cap; modest confidence given consumer sensitivity to rising unemployment.
Defensive staple outperforms in late-cycle slowdown; rising unemployment (+0.30 y/y) and steepening curve favor the sector.
Steeper 2s10s (+88bp y/y) helps NIM, but softening labor market and potential credit deterioration offset; net neutral.
Falling yields are supportive but extreme valuation makes macro tailwind secondary to idiosyncratic AI demand; no strong macro edge.
Consumer-facing revenue at risk from rising unemployment, partially offset by duration tailwind from lower yields.
Defensive characteristics are positive, but healthcare is more policy-driven than macro-driven; limited conviction from macro data alone.
Classic late-cycle cyclical faces headwinds from rising unemployment and decelerating nominal growth; curve steepening signals slowdown ahead.
Energy needs accelerating growth and inflation; 2.4% CPI and softening labor market argue against that backdrop.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and JPM Shine While UNH, AAPL, and PG Absorb Sharp Negative Reactions
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available today. MSFT's +7.6% move on its 4/30 results is the strongest positive tone shift in the group, suggesting the market narrative around cloud/AI spend is being validated. JPM's +4.0% reaction on 4/11 earnings similarly reflects an improving tone for financials that may still have room to run. On the negative side, UNH's catastrophic -22.4% drop on 4/17 earnings followed by a C-suite departure on 4/29 signals a deeply broken narrative that I do not think has stabilized yet. AAPL's -3.7% reaction to its 5/1 results and PG's -3.7% on 4/24 both suggest crowded expectations met with disappointment, though the magnitude is more modest and may already be priced.

views.note: The +7.6% earnings reaction is the strongest positive sentiment shift in the universe, indicating a narrative upgrade that likely has follow-through.
A +4.0% earnings pop and multiple subsequent 8-K filings suggest constructive institutional tone; the positive reaction was decisive and clean.
A -22.4% earnings collapse followed by a senior officer departure signals a severe narrative break that is unlikely to reverse quickly.
The -3.7% post-earnings drop on 5/1 suggests sentiment is turning negative, though the magnitude is moderate enough that it could stabilize.
The -3.7% earnings reaction on 4/24 was sharp but the subsequent 5/1 filing (Other Events) may indicate management is addressing concerns; I lack conviction either way.
A +1.7% earnings reaction on 4/24 is modestly positive and the steady cadence of 8-K filings suggests a stable-to-improving narrative.
The flat -0.1% reaction to 5/1 earnings is a non-event from a sentiment perspective; no clear directional signal.
A muted +0.6% earnings reaction on 4/30 and two officer-change filings in April leave the sentiment picture ambiguous.
No earnings reaction data available; the only recent filings are an officer change and an Other Events 8-K, providing no clear sentiment direction.
No earnings price reaction in the data; recent filings are routine corporate governance and Reg FD disclosures with no sentiment catalyst.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty at Extreme Levels Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Across Export-Sensitive and China-Exposed Names
memos.body: I am writing with high concern: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has surged to 890.82, up nearly 248% over three months, while VIX sits at 24.60 (+50% over the same period) and HY OAS has widened 110bp to 3.78%—a combination that in my experience reflects not transient noise but a structural shift in the policy environment, likely driven by escalating trade/tariff actions and export-control tightening. NVDA's mid-April 8-K (8.01 Other Events) is consistent with a material disclosure potentially related to export-control restrictions on advanced AI chips to China, which I view as a durable headwind. WTI crude at $60.59, down ~17% in three months, suggests demand-destruction fears or OPEC+ discipline breakdown, which pressures XOM's earnings power but also signals global growth anxiety that weighs on CAT's international order book. I have higher conviction in domestically oriented defensives like PG and JPM, where policy risk is more manageable, and lower conviction in names with heavy China/semiconductor supply-chain exposure until we see clarity on whether current export controls tighten further or stabilize.

views.note: Mid-April 8-K likely tied to export-control developments on AI chips to China; structural policy headwind until controls are clarified or relaxed.
Massive China manufacturing and sales exposure makes AAPL vulnerable to any further tariff escalation or retaliatory action amid record policy uncertainty.
WTI down 17% in 3 months and policy uncertainty at extremes suggest weakening global capex cycle, pressuring CAT's international backlog.
WTI at $60.59 compresses margins, but XOM's domestic production base limits direct geopolitical exposure; I'd wait for oil to stabilize before adding.
Defensive consumer staples with pricing power and limited direct export-control exposure; multiple Reg FD filings suggest proactive investor communication amid uncertainty.
Widening yield curve (+25bp in 1m) supports NII, and JPM's domestic focus insulates it from direct trade-war fallout, though credit spreads widening warrants monitoring.
Flurry of 8-K filings (four since mid-March) may reflect regulatory or antitrust developments; policy uncertainty is elevated but GOOGL's revenue base is less China-dependent than hardware peers.
Cross-border e-commerce and AWS infrastructure could face tariff and data-sovereignty headwinds, but diversified revenue limits single-policy exposure.

plan.summary: Concentrate in MSFT, JPM, and GOOGL where analyst views converge on strong fundamentals, positive momentum, and favorable sentiment, while keeping a meaningful cash buffer given extreme policy uncertainty (EPU ~891) and elevated VIX. Avoid UNH, AAPL, XOM, and CAT where multiple analysts flag structural or cyclical headwinds.

plans.rationale: Strongest consensus across all five analysts: Technical (best 4w/12w relative strength, +7.6% earnings pop), Fundamentals (revenue +13.3%, net margin 36.9%), Macro (duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields), and Sentiment (strongest positive post-earnings reaction). RSI at 72 is the only caution, warranting a moderate stop.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 390 (roughly 10% drawdown) or a reversal in 10y yields above 4.60% would negate the thesis.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst's top pick (cleanest uptrend, above both MAs, low ATR), Sentiment analyst notes clean +4.0% earnings pop, and Geopolitics analyst highlights domestic focus insulating from trade-war fallout. Fundamentals analyst is neutral due to macro credit sensitivity, so I size slightly below MSFT.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 240 or HY OAS widening above 4.50% signaling credit stress would trigger reassessment.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst's second-highest conviction (net margin 38.3%, net income +46% YoY), Macro analyst favors as duration-sensitive growth, and Sentiment notes modestly positive +1.7% earnings reaction. Technical analyst is neutral (middling setup, below 200d), so I size below the top two names.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 155 (roughly 5.5% below current) or antitrust ruling materially restricting ad business would change my view.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst is constructive (net income nearly doubled, margin expansion to 10.7%), but Technical (21.5% off highs, weak 12w relative strength), Sentiment (flat earnings reaction), and Macro/Geopolitics analysts are all neutral. Small position reflects the fundamental upside potential tempered by lack of confirming signals.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below 175 or unemployment rising above 4.5% pressuring consumer spending would trigger exit.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals are extraordinary (56.2% net margin, 78% revenue growth), but Geopolitics analyst flags export-control headwind at high conviction (0.80 avoid), and Technical/Sentiment analysts are neutral with no clear catalyst. Tiny position captures potential upside if export concerns prove manageable.
plans.changes_my_mind: Confirmation of new China export restrictions on H20/B-series chips or a close below 105 would trigger exit.
